title: Prefetch & Chunking — Heuristic Explorer and Safe-Mode Walkthrough
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Design a Heuristic Explorer UI inside Redwood Console that surfaces automatic prefetch/prefill and chunking recommendations, visualizes cost/latency tradeoffs, and provides a safe-mode guardrail (rollback/on-call friendly).
background: Teams repeatedly tune caching and batching but lack a safe, explainable UI for testing changes across workloads.
Current console screens expose low-level knobs (batch size, cache ttl, prefix caching) but do not convey expected user-visible impact or rollback guidance.
Objective is to give operators a lightweight exploration workspace where they can preview recommended heuristics, simulate 1–10k rps workloads, and generate conservative runbooks for rollouts.
design_goals: Surface clear recommendations (what to change + expected delta in p95 latency and token cost)
Make changes reversible with one-click safe rollback and canary guidance
Explain why a recommendation exists (heuristic trace) so SREs can trust automated suggestions
Provide an interactive simulator to estimate cost/latency across traffic mixes
Keep primary flow accessible to PMs and product engineers (short copy, visual cues), while surfacing an advanced panel for power users (detailed metrics and kernel scheduling notes).
user_stories: As an SRE, I want a recommended prefetch/prefill strategy that I can preview on a representative prompt set so I can validate regressions before rollout.
As a product engineer, I want a conservative (safe-mode) preset that prioritizes correctness and minimal extra token usage for canary rollouts.
As a platform owner, I want to see a cost/latency curve for each recommendation to make trade-off decisions with stakeholders.
As an operator, I want to store the recommendation as a named policy and link it to a rollout plan (canary percent, time window, fallback model).
proposal: Introduce a new Console panel called 'Heuristic Explorer' under Model > Optimization. The panel has three vertical sections: (1) Recommendations list (left) with short rationale pills and confidence scores; (2) Interactive simulator (center) where users can load a sample workload or upload prompts and run a fast simulation producing delta estimates for p50/p95 latency and per-1000-token cost; (3) Advanced inspector (right) showing the heuristic trace (why this prefilling/chunking suggestion), kernel compatibility notes, and an action rail with 'Apply as Policy', 'Create Canary', 'Export Runbook'. Add a 'Safe Mode' toggle that switches recommendations to conservative variants and locks auto-aggressive prefetching above a token budget threshold.
design_assets: Copy deck: Confluence > Console UX > Heuristic Explorer copy (v1.3)
engineering_notes: Simulator will call runtime-sim service (sim-v1) with a sample of token distributions; needs feature flag 'sim-heuristics'
Recommendation list computed by optimizer service (opt-heuristics v2) and must include 'confidence' and 'explain_trace' fields
Safe Mode enforces token-budget floor — runtime must reject applied policies that exceed configured per-request extra-token budget
Backend must store named policies in policy-store with versioning and a rollback endpoint
Telemetry: record show/apply/cancel events, simulator runs, and modeled vs. actual post-rollout deltas for audit and ML feedback
acceptance_criteria: Design mocks for desktop and tablet completed and handed off to frontend
Clickable prototype demonstrates: loading a sample workload, running a simulation, switching Safe Mode, and exporting a runbook
PM and Eng have approved the interaction flow and the action rail labels
E2E story for a canary creation using the 'Apply as Policy' action is documented with required API contract fields
Copy and microcopy passes localization check (EN/FR/DE)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly aggressive recommendations may increase customer token bill — Mitigation: Safe Mode defaults to conservative presets and we expose estimated extra tokens in simulation
Risk: Simulator estimates differ from production — Mitigation: implement telemetry to compare predicted vs observed within first 24h of rollout and surface regression alerts
Risk: Confusing UI for new users — Mitigation: include a guided first-run walkthrough and contextual explainers on hover
open_questions: What sampling window should the simulator use by default (1k requests, 10k, or last 24h)?
Do we allow policy application to cross model-family boundaries (e.g., fallback to cheaper quantized variant)?
Should 'explain_trace' be surfaced as human-friendly bullets or an expandable raw JSON view for SREs?
What SLO guardrails do we require before enabling auto-suggested canaries for P0 customers?
review_comments: PM (Rachel Ng, 2026-02-25): Love the simulator. Ask: can we add an annotation step to tie a recommendation to a product experiment ID?
Eng (Luis Ortega, 2026-03-02): Backend needs to rate-limit simulator calls to avoid load on sim-v1. Suggest batch simulation endpoints.
SRE (Jenna Moore, 2026-03-04): Add a pre-apply dry-run mode that will create a temporary policy and run a 1-hour shadow test against a 1% sample before canary.
Design peer (Tom Becker, 2026-03-06): UI copy for confidence scores should avoid numeric-only labels; propose 'High / Medium / Low + short reason'.
